opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires role ownership of the system, which does not apply here. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security check: E034 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits the max to read. Requested write is above the max, so recommend read.
reason: Matthew Mejia (E034) requests write access to Payroll. Security records indicate E034 is a contractor with basic security training, which limits contractors to read (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed for contractors). The requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted. The HR note claiming full-time status conflicts with the security database lookup, and the restrictive security-based determination applies here. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and E034 is an Analyst, so admin would not apply in any case.
